memo.verdict: Park. Bearish on the return against the framework's 20 percent a year bar; conviction medium. HELLENiQ Energy (ELPE-GR) at EUR 18.18 (2026-10-02) is a well-executed, fully priced cyclical margin upswing: the 'Modal return' is about -18.4 percent a year to 2028-04-02 and -4.9 percent a year to 2029-10-02. The gate on management ('No mediocre management' C), business quality ('Business' C), predictability ('Transmission' B) and trackability ('Leading indicators' A) does not park the case; it is parked on its return. Conviction is medium rather than high because momentum (relative strength at the 99th percentile; technical momentum B; sell-side momentum A) can carry a peak multiple longer than fundamentals warrant and the next two prints are likely to be strong; conviction is high on the direction of the earnings path from FY2027, which the sell-side's own median path shares. Condition for a re-run: the shares falling toward the EUR 9 to 10 clearing price with estimates cut and the multiple below 7.5x, when 'Trough on Trough' becomes the setup to test.
case: The thesis. HELLENiQ Energy is a well-run Greek duopoly refiner riding the strongest external force in the universe this year, the middle-distillate margin spike after the Strait of Hormuz closure of late February 2026, and the force has travelled every layer of the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain into the sell-side's estimates. At EUR 18.18 the shares pay for the margin to last into 2028 and for a peak multiple to hold while it does, so the modal return is negative over both horizons. A compelling business story and not an investment case at this price.

The change is external, supply-driven, cyclical and at full strength. Hormuz, Russian refinery outages and two decades of European underinvestment took the realised margin from USD 13.80 per barrel (Q2 2025) to USD 20.50 (Q1 2026) to USD 22.50 (Q2 2026), the highest since Q4 2022. The margin carries about 65 percent of estimated forward earnings-per-share sensitivity; the internal forces together about a tenth. Every Mediterranean refiner captured it (Motor Oil USD 192 per tonne, Tupras USD 21.40 per barrel, MOL USD 20.80), which makes the pattern sector-level and the multiple industry-driven. Durability is contested: the chief executive expects margins elevated through 2027 and potentially 2028; the dominant broker's base case normalises to long-term averages by 2027; the risks report projects benchmark margins reverting to USD 5 to 6 per barrel by 2027. The two-plus years' visibility the framework asks for is met on the company's view, not the most cautious house's.

Direction by force ('External forces' B): demand neutral to headwind domestically (Greek demand -6 percent in Q2 2026 to 1.5 million tonnes) and a tailwind in export distillates (international marketing volumes +21.5 percent in 1H 2026); competition easing in refining and tightening in Greek power retail (PPC 50 percent, Metlen 21, the Motor Oil and GEK Terna alliance 17, Enerwave 6.34); disruption a headwind to the renewables leg (Greek solar curtailment 7.5 percent in 2025, 12 percent projected for 2026); political and regulatory a strong headwind (retail margin caps re-imposed 11 March 2026; no visibility on a 2H 2026 windfall tax; the FY2023 solidarity contribution cost EUR 222.4m gross; CO2 deficit accrual EUR 209m at 30 June 2026; pump discounts of EUR 0.10 and EUR 0.05 per litre exceeding a EUR 20m budget); supply mixed (20 to 25 percent of crude came through Hormuz; the group ran at 103 percent on substitute grades; VLCC spot earnings about USD 246,000 a day in August 2026 against USD 54,000 in 2025; Brent averaged USD 92.90 per barrel in 1H 2026 and USD 105 in Q2); macro mixed (a 5 percent EUR/USD move is about 9 percent of earnings per share; 80 percent of operating costs in euro; gross-margin currency exposure unhedged; Greek GDP 1.9 percent against 0.9 percent for the euro area); the inventory valuation effect (EUR 408m gain in Q2 2026 after a EUR 329m loss in FY2025) material to perception and to the mixed-basis consensus mean, not to cash earning power.
counter_case: At its strongest: European refining is in a structural golden age, not a cyclical one. Europe imports 35 percent of its jet fuel and 20 percent of its diesel after two decades of underinvestment; Western European capacity keeps closing; new Atlantic-basin plants are slow to start; the Mediterranean sulphur emission control area added about 100,000 barrels a day of marine gasoil demand from May 2025; record diesel premiums of USD 79.95 per barrel over Dated Brent were printed as late as mid-July 2026; Hormuz hostilities re-escalated in July. On this view realised margins hold at USD 18 to 22 per barrel through 2028, FY2027 and FY2028 adjusted earnings per share stay near 2.40 EUR, FY2029 earnings per share is 2.5 to 3.0 EUR, and at 8.5x the shares are worth 21 to 25 EUR plus dividends, clearing the bar. The chief executive, who has been right about his market so far, expects margins elevated through 2027 and potentially 2028, above the dominant broker's base case. The power pillar reaches EUR 300m of EBITDA by 2030 with Romanian and Bulgarian returns of 10 to 12 percent that even the risks report found inconsistent with its bear profile, and re-rates the group toward a utility-weighted 9x to 10x. Eight of nine brokers are still raising, so the sell-side is catching up, not leading. Meanwhile the balance sheet (1.3x; 97 percent of gross debt under committed facilities) and a 4 to 5 percent dividend bound the downside, and the Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 prints will be strong enough to carry the multiple through any normalisation, so a holder collects the yield while the market decides.

Read as 'Major Corporate Change' rather than 'Demand Inflection': Enerwave, the Geneva desk, the Skopje pipeline, the Romanian pivot and a renewed management are a multi-dimensional internal change at full output along the chain, and the fit deserves C or better.
triggers: - Margin durability, the question the case turns on: our side is a fade to about USD 20 per barrel in 2H 2026, about USD 15 in FY2027 and USD 13 to 14 from FY2028 (probable); the bull side is at or above USD 18 through FY2027 with FY2027 adjusted earnings per share at or above 2.40 EUR (about one in three). Alarm: realised margin below USD 15 per barrel in any quarter. Invalidate for the bull reading: two consecutive quarters below USD 15 (the earnings review's checkpoint, February 2027). Invalidate for our view: realised above USD 18 through FY2027 with FY2027 earnings per share at or above 2.40 EUR; what would change our mind is two consecutive quarters above USD 18 after the Q4 2026 print with no Hormuz normalisation and FY2027 consensus rising.

- The multiple: our side is a de-rating to about 8.0x (probable); the bull side is above 9x through 2027 (about one in four). Alarm: below 8.40x (the de-rating has begun). Invalidate for our view: above 10x sustained through 2027 alongside an announced step-up in the power platform's earnings tracking to EUR 300m by 2030.
- Euro-dollar: modal 1.15 to 1.18, a modest headwind; alarm at 1.20 (the risks report's bear case); Maybank 1.18 by Q2 2027, Allianz 1.19.

- Margin normalisation drivers: global capacity additions (about 1,000 thousand barrels a day net in 2026), Hormuz transit volumes (alarm: back to pre-conflict levels), Chinese export quotas, Russian refinery restarts.

- Greek state intervention: a windfall levy on FY2026 profits is plausible, roughly even, a one-off of a few hundred million euro, treated in cash and dividend thinking rather than the adjusted earnings path; alarm: a bill tabled; what would change our mind: a legislative statement either way. Caps persist.

- Renewables return dilution: our side is that the pillar earns near, not above, its 7.90 to 8.20 percent cost of capital (Greek assets mid-single-digit, Romanian and Bulgarian 10 to 12 percent); alarm: blended capture below 85 percent of spot, or under 1,000 MW operating at 1H 2027; what would change our mind: over 1,000 MW at 1H 2027 with capture above 85 percent and over 35 percent of capacity outside Greece by FY2027, which would move the fair multiple toward the conceded 9.0x.
